introduction_claim: India already has national-scale digital policing infrastructure through CCTNS.
CCTNS digitizes FIRs chargesheets and related police processes.
CCTNS data is replicated near-real-time at the National Data Centre.
CCTNS uses standardized investigation forms and master codes.
ICJS connects police courts prisons forensics and prosecution.
Sensitive police and criminal-justice records require contextual authorization and reviewable disclosure.
notes: This is a research motivation, not an official stated conclusion.

introduction_claim: ABAC evaluates subject object action and environment attributes against policy.
ABAC is relevant to cross-organization information sharing while retaining control.
Permissioned blockchain is suitable for known organizations compared with open public-chain participation.
notes: Phrase as candidate suitability, not universal best.

introduction_claim: Blockchain can support tamper-evident audit and access-control properties but does not make data private by itself.
Digital evidence blockchain literature exists, so the novelty is not blockchain evidence management alone.
Fabric plus ABAC has already been studied in generic data-sharing contexts.
Law-enforcement XAI needs stakeholder-aware explanations and must account for automation-bias risks.
High-stakes decisions should prefer interpretable models where feasible.
Predictive-policing data can create feedback-loop risks.
notes: Use to explain why paper is not individual prediction.

introduction_claim: Public NCRB data should be treated as aggregate reported/registered crime context, not individual police-record data.
SEBA-XAI keeps raw sensitive records off-chain and stores commitments for requests policies approvals models and explanations.
notes: No external citation needed but mark as proposal.
